daily_brief: US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to visit Moscow and Kyiv this weekend carrying a new proposal to end the Ukraine war, with President Zelensky confirming he will meet them Sunday after their talks with Putin [BBC, France 24]. The diplomatic push comes as Russia struck Ukraine's SBU security headquarters in Kyiv with a precision drone aimed at the security chief's office, prompting Zelensky to order a retaliatory response [BBC]. Tensions between the US and Iran escalated sharply as explosions were reported near Iran's crucial Kharg Island oil terminal, with Iranian media alleging a US strike on an oil tanker—though neither government has confirmed the reports [France 24, The Hindu]. In Europe, Volkswagen's board approved plans to cut an additional 50,000 jobs, bringing total planned reductions to 100,000 by 2030 amid fierce competition from Chinese automakers [BBC]. Meanwhile, the UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to formally move away from the Mercator map projection in favor of the Equal Earth design, with only the US opposing the African-led initiative to more accurately represent the continent's true size [The Guardian, The Hindu, RFI].

top_stories.headline: Trump Envoys Head to Moscow and Kyiv with New Peace Proposal as Ukraine War Intensifies
bullets: US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia Saturday to meet Putin, then travel to Ukraine Sunday to meet Zelensky
Trump confirmed the envoys are carrying 'a proposal to end the war' between Russia and Ukraine
Earlier Friday, a Russian drone struck the SBU headquarters in Kyiv, targeting security chief Oleksandr Poklad's office; Zelensky ordered a retaliatory response
Zelensky said he would guarantee Russian airspace safety during the envoys' visit and called on Russia to reciprocate for Ukraine

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the precision of the drone strike and its implications for escalation before talks

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief coverage focused on the diplomatic mission

sources.name: The Economist
sources.framing_note: Broader analysis framing the war as 'intensifying, expanding and stuck'

top_stories.headline: Explosions Reported Near Iran's Kharg Island Oil Hub Amid Renewed US-Iran Hostilities
bullets: Iranian media reported multiple explosions near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export terminal in the Gulf
Semi-official Tasnim and Nournews agencies claimed a US missile strike hit an Iranian oil tanker; no casualties reported
Neither US nor Iranian officials have officially confirmed the reports
Fighting between the US and Iran resumed last Sunday, with Iran claiming retaliatory strikes on US bases in Kuwait and the UAE

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Presented as breaking news with emphasis on unconfirmed nature of reports

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Provided context on six-month US-Iran conflict and ongoing Strait of Hormuz tensions

top_stories.headline: Volkswagen Approves Plan to Cut 100,000 Jobs by 2030 in Historic Restructuring
bullets: VW board approved cutting an additional 50,000 jobs, bringing total planned reductions to 100,000 by 2030
The company is considering the future of four German plants amid falling sales and competition from Chinese brands
VW will reduce its model lineup by 50% by 2035 and cut product complexity by 75%
Shares rose approximately 7% in Frankfurt following the announcement

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Described as 'biggest restructuring in the group's almost nine-decade history'

top_stories.headline: UN Votes to Phase Out Mercator Map in Favor of Projection Showing Africa's True Size
bullets: The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to adopt a resolution promoting the Equal Earth projection over the traditional Mercator map
The US was the sole vote against, calling the resolution 'superfluous' and an 'ideological agenda'; six countries abstained
France announced it would stop using Mercator maps in its Foreign Ministry, adopting projections 'more faithful to actual surface areas'
The non-binding resolution was led by Togo on behalf of the African Union to counter perceptions that Africa is peripheral

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the cultural and educational impact of cartographic distortions

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Focused on US opposition characterizing it as 'ideological agenda'

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Highlighted France's decision as part of broader French foreign policy shift toward Africa

top_stories.headline: Russia Blamed for Escalating Sabotage Campaign Targeting European Military Sites
bullets: Germany's interior minister declared 'Russia is responsible' for explosive-laden drones found at Leipzig airport in August
A series of suspicious fires hit defense facilities across Europe in August, from Italy to Estonia
Poland's interior minister warned Russia is 'intensifying its activities, including terrorist and sabotage activities'
Russia denies involvement, with Putin demanding proof and officials calling accusations 'absurd'

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive overview connecting multiple incidents across Europe as part of coordinated campaign
